variant: automation kit and vacuum attachment on a standard excavator
name: Xpanner X1 Panel Lift
specialisedFor: utility-scale solar construction: lifting PV modules and placing them on tracker racking
summary: Automation kit for a standard excavator that carries the PV panel box, picks modules straight from it with vacuum and places them, so a three-person crew only aligns and fastens. Released in July 2026 and offered on subscription; it joins Xpanner's X1 piling kits.

germany.statusNote: No German or European seller or project found. Xpanner sells from Santa Fe Springs, California, on an all-inclusive subscription (hardware, kit and licence, Xpanner Connect software, on-site support); no price published.

specs.label: Workflow
specs.value: transports the PV panel box, picks panels from it and installs them with one excavator; no separate loader or forklift
specs.quote: X1 transports the PV panel box, picks panels directly from the box, and installs them using a single excavator.

specs.label: Crew
specs.conditions: crew handles machine operation and panel installation

specs.label: Rows worked
specs.conditions: left and right of the machine at once
specs.quote: Machine workstwo rows simultaneously,left and right.

specs.label: Sensors
specs.value: LiDAR, vision and GNSS fused into a live 3D model of the site
specs.quote: The system fuses data from LIDAR, vision, and GNSS sensors to build a live 3D model of the jobsite

specs.label: Operation
specs.value: one-button assisted automation with automated vacuum handling and simple remote operation
specs.quote: Automated vacuum handlingAssisted panel positioningSimple remote operation with easy interface

specs.label: Controller
specs.quote: Mango is Xpanner’s core technology—designed for real-time decision-making and precision control across hydraulic, electric, and mechanical systems, all within a robust RTOS environment.

notes: Kit on a standard excavator (crawler tracks assumed); the vacuum lifting attachment is the gripper.
Assisted automation: the operator stays in control and the crew aligns, fastens and checks the modules.
Remote operation keeps people out of the load path during lifts.
